Brawlhalla.Comment: As much as I want to give this game a negative review, I cannot justifiably do so. Most people who play this game will stay at a basic, casual level and never even notice or be forced to encounter the serious passivity problem this game has. So, despite my frustration with Brawlhalla, I am giving it a positive review. My recommendation would be to play with your friends and avoid taking this game too seriously. However, the prevalence of the passive float meta is noticeable as early as high platinum/low diamond, so be very forewarned and prepared to deal with it if you intend to play this game for many hours.

This game is unbelievably amazing if your sole purpose in life is to have a sweaty, fat 12-year-old plow their scythe up your anal cavity and rip out all vital organs. Brawhalla's vast range of unique combos and weapons exhibits such robust creativity to the extent that players only require two brain cells to be godly in this game! Furthermore, Brawhalla’s community is truly the pinnacle of gaming culture, where many players demonstrate good sportsmanship through a variety of fun emojis! And occasionally, players wish to further connect by inviting you to custom lobbies, to enact thoughtful exchanges with one another! I am starting to lose count of the amount of times I have been told to kill myself!! This game’s only made me break two monitors! Only two!! If that’s not considered a steal, then I don’t know what is! Another positive aspect I feel is overlooked is its mysterious attributes. I will never know the degree of skill my opponent is going to have despite the claimed “accuracy” of ELO rating! Hell, I was at 1965 and plummeted back to gold! And I still got paired with Diamond Ranks! This obscure inconsistency adds a whole new excitement as I do not know what the ♥♥♥♥ I am going to do to myself after a match! I am very appreciative of the experience Brawhalla has provided me, as it has excavated whole new emotions that I had yet to discover. To summarize, if you’re looking for that extra push to jump off that cliff or bridge, then this is the game for you!

As someone who has played this game ever since 2016, I was able to see the changes the game went through. Upon initial release, it looked very promising especially for a time where smash was the only dominant fighting game. Playing the game, it was fun to have a combo based fighting game but also making combos balanced with the option to dodge. However, in the state it has been in, it's hard to ignore the issues the competitive scene may have. I'm sure if you are a brawlhalla player, you have probably complained about passive players at least once (even with not many hours). The dodge mechanic makes passive play awfully common and rewarding in this game; hardly even worth going in unless against significantly worse players. If you want a good visual of what I am talking about, literally watch ANY tournament not played by sandstorm or any other notoriously good players and the issue with dodge becomes more apparent. BMG has attempted to make dodge more balanced by increasing and reducing the cooldown on dodge dependent on if it's grounded, air, etc. But it still haunts this game. Don't get me wrong, there are definitely still ways to enjoy the competitive scene without playing passive but passive play is just sadly more rewarding in this game. Again, as for someone who has clocked nearly 800 hrs across multiple platforms, it's hard for me to recommend this to newer fighting game players and even a few veterans. I do truly hope this game fixes the issues with passive play but for now, I can not recommend this game in its current state.

Brawlhalla is a game I'm cursed to care about and keep returning to like Destiny.

It’s tempting to view Nintendo’s Super Smash Bros. franchise as one of a kind. But recently, other games have attempted to capture that same accessible blend of platforming and fighting. If you enjoy Smash Bros. gameplay, but for some reason dislike Nintendo characters, you have options. Originally released in 2017, following a beta in 2015, Brawlhalla remains the alternative platform fighter with perhaps the most staying power. The free-to-play game sports a unique and approachable, if unpolished, set of fighting mechanics that appeals to even veteran Smash fans. Nintendo Switch owners should still stick to Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, as that game doesn’t lock the bulk of its content behind paywalls. However, as a crossplay-friendly console, mobile, and PC game, Brawlhalla is the platform fighter for the rest of us.

There must be a counter to this obvious inbalance? Yes there is, it comes in the form of throwing your weapon. Throwing your weapon will hitstun the opponent and allow you to re-equip and attack the opponent within the same frame. Due to the fact that there is no priority, deflection or parry systems in this game it ends up devolving into who can throw their weapon the most. An excellent read followed up by a perfectively timed smash is all made pointless when the enemy throws their weapon at you at the last second with no punishment available for such an audacious and should-be-punishable move. I could go on forever about the games combat flaws but honestly for a free to play game it is good fun but very shallow. I don't recommend taking this game seriously as a competitive fighter as you will disappointed with the shallow button mashing, weapon throwing facade it turns into at high levels of play.

In 2021 you would think one of the biggest fighting games on Steam would at the very least have decent optimization as people have 4k monitors. Nope, no chance, not Brawlhalla. It's honestly astonishing how a game that's been around since 2017 with a dev team that's backed by Ubisoft has such piss poor optimization. In the game there's no way to change your screen resolution or graphics settings, all you can do is change it from Full Screen to either Maximized or Windowed. Unfortunately, that can cause input delays and that's horrible for any online fighter. I know it's a long shot, but maybe by 2031 Brawlhalla will finally have optimization that even old indie titles with single developers have in their games.

Another huge problem is the community. Higher ranked people are nice and will actually try to help you, but in ranks like gold and silver, almost everyone is a jerk. When you lose, they'll brag and spam a phrase to make fun of you, even if they only beat you by a little. If you win, they'll call you out for spamming or just complain and say you got lucky. It makes for an overall toxic community with players staring out. Brawlhalla is a free game though, so perhaps I should not harshly criticize it. It can be fun for a few hours at most, but the core concepts of the game make for bland, repetitive and clunky gameplay, and the community will just make you mad.

There’s just so much here, and I’ve rarely seen a game with so many enjoyable and replayable ideas in a single package. Playing eight-player matches and classic two-player brawls are only the beginning, and I don’t see a reason to stop playing Brawlhalla for a long time.

Brawlhalla is a fighting game heavily based on Super Smash Bros: you control a character and you have to beat up to other 3 players, hitting an enemy will make their damage go higher: the higher the damage the further they'll get knocked back with strong attacks, get pushed off the stage and you lose. However the main differences between this game and Smash Bros are the much more fast paced gameplay, the presence of full working weapons (picking a glowing sword will give your character one of the 2 random weapons they can use, each one will completely change and improve your moves) with incredibly different effects, nice stages (all pretty harmless with the exception of a few moving platforms here and there, making each battle a lot more skill-based compared to Smash's hazardous stages), funny extra gamemodes (like one the resembles American Football where you have to bring a ball to the opponent's goal and another one where you are given an endless amount of snowballs as the only attack, actually turning the battle in an hilarious snowball fight) and amazing graphics and sountrack all make Brawlhalla a must-have for any fan of Super Smash Bros or fighting games in general.

Perhaps best of all, it’s totally free, so you really don’t have anything to lose by giving it a try. At worst, you’ll find a Smash clone that doesn’t have a ton of new ideas; at best, you’ll find a new go-to for when you have a few friends over for a gaming session.

Brawlhalla is a fun, accessible platform fighter that has something for both casual players and those looking for competitive action. While its monetization model can be grindy, and some matchmaking issues may detract from the experience, the game’s diverse roster, fluid gameplay, and frequent updates make it a strong contender in the genre. Whether you're playing casually with friends or climbing the ranked ladder, Brawlhalla offers plenty of value for players looking for an exciting, free-to-play brawler.

Great game, but was ruined by the devs, salty players, and updates in general. I started playing this game back in 2015, when it first went into open beta, and I used to play it a lot and really enjoyed it, but I pretty much just gave up on it when Ragnir (the dragon legend) came out. This game had a lot of potential and now it's rubbish. I've lost my patience with this game, to be honest. Every legend that came out after Ulgrim has either been broken, over-powered, or both (usually both). The game is very unbalanced at this point. New legends get all the attention while the old legends are neglected and most are completely outshined by the new ones. Most of the old legends, especially the classic ones (from Bodvar to Teros) have simple, extremely basic moves that can't even compare to the signatures of the new legends (e.g. usually just a simple swing of a weapon for old legend signatures). By contrast, newer legends (legends that came out after Ulgrim) have strong, fancy, detailed signatures/movesets that have a lot of range, are fast, and/or do a lot of damage, and so they're much stronger and are much easier to spam. Some of the newer legends even have unique abilities no other legend has, and while that isn't bad in and of itself, it ruins the balance of the game since older legends don't have unique abilities. And yet, the devs just seem to be neglecting older legends and don't revamp them, balance things out, or anything (and no, adjusting a single hitbox or boosting knockback by 1 does not count as "balancing," so don't try to say they aren't neglecting older legends). And we haven't even gotten to weapon balance (swords outclass most other weapons, spears are easy to spam, etc., and this has been a problem for a long time), older weapons versus newer weapons (gauntlets and now scythe, especially), the extremely toxic community (almost as toxic as Rumble Fighter's community), the intense lag (you can literally be attacking your opponent one moment and suiciding the next without knowing what's happening, among other things), etc. Overall, the game could've been so much fun and had a lot of potential, but the devs seem to have just screwed it up and haven't really listened to the community's complaints, mostly because the toxic players outnumber the other members of the community and are louder than they are, and that's because most of the other players have left BECAUSE of the toxic community, so it's just a cycle in that sense, where toxic players come, other players leave because of the toxic players, more toxic players come, and the cycle repeats. The game also isn't very friendly toward rookies. Most people that I knew that used to play this game during its earlier stages ("veteran players," if you will) seem to have just quit playing. I made it to Diamond (the highest rank) and I can't even say I'm proud of that accomplishment, since it really wasn't worth it. I could say more, but I think I've made my point. I can't recommend this game anymore. It's still free to play, but it's definitely no longer fun to play.

OK, first of all I have played this game for months and am Gold in both 1v1s and 2v2s. I have many hours in smash bros and a few in Rivals of Aether but I have always loved Brawlhalla. This game is appealing for its simplicity and fast paced gameplay. Observing reviews I've seen a lot of complaining about spamming and to that I say spamming is equaly prevalent in most other platform fighters.  My friends introduced me to this game as a way for my smash playing friends and I to play a game like this with friends that don't play smash. At first that is all it was, a smash substitute of sorts, but as I improved and learned the controls my relationship with this game evolved and I was grinding the game even when my friends weren't online to play with. The legends are all very well balanced partly because of the similar sized hurtboxes and similar speed, attack, and defense stats. Another reason I rarely get salty because "the other legend is just too OP against mine" is because each legend essentially has 2 built-in play styles in the form of their 2 weapons. This means that if you are struggling with one weapon, the other weapon might not have such a hard time. Coming from Smash Ultimate I was used to one-off approaches and far from true combos but this game allows for much faster paced gameplay and combos if you use the right characters. The devs truly love this game and give it regular updates as well as supporting the eSports scene greatly. For people who truly dislike this genre of game, this game might not change that, but to people who just haven't found a platform fighter that interests them I would say to try this game and get a few hours in.

Committing yourself to enjoying this game and learning how to play it, will always be the start to finding your passion for it. However you decide to play this game such as a joke, for fun, competitively, or just to battle your friends I know for a fact that you won't want to let go. Actually understanding this game sparks a desire to understand more about it, and to practice, learn, play, lose, win, flex, enjoy, share, and connect through this free-to-play fighting game developed as Brawlhalla. For a lot of people, this community and game becomes apart of their childhood, life, hobbies, Content, and even their job. For me the nostalgic feeling of Brawlhalla reminds me of when I first opened it on my first hour. interested and curious of how I could become something in Brawlhalla so then Brawlhalla could become something I feel is apart of me. From all the friendships I've created, to all the wholesome post-game conversations I've encountered. There's always a light side to look at when playing Brawl. I have played the game for almost a year now and currently have more then 2,000 hours on record. I've played while being open with a passion to be the better player I always know I can become. Interested in tournaments and Discord servers it becomes so easy to sink into Brawls welcoming community. With amazing content creators, friendly players, and very skilled professionals when you look in through the window you might finally realize you aren't outside, and in fact outside is through the door you could never find, until your spark of an interest let you find the way. The small and hidden aspects of Brawlhalla are what let it establish it's unknown qualities while being known for as a seemingly upfront free-to-play. The part of my life history that relates to brawlhalla will be remembered until I no longer have any memory at all. I seek for more in the depths of high tier game-play and communities as for now and the future. I'm not sure when I'll let go of a such a loving hobby and passion, and I'm not looking forward to. I truly hope others and more can experience Brawlhalla the way I did, with hope for prosperity and the scope for communion. People who read all of this will already have enough devotion to spark an interest in the game I've loved so dearly. Thank you.

The amount of time I've spent in this game would be surprising considering the score I'm giving it, but I cannot seriously recommend Brawlhalla when there are so many better ways to use your time. There's NO community in any online game I've faced (not even other F2P games such as LoL) that is as toxic as this one is. If you don't live close to one of the servers for this game your connection is jsut utter garbage. You're always gona have some sort of input lag. If you've ever played any fighting game you'll realize this game is very unbalanced and devs just cycle through metas to hype the tournaments up basically as they know exactly what they're doing and it's not balance. There's no penalty for doing or not doing stuff here (NO Rock Paper Scissors type of design you find in literally EVERY OTHER FIGHTING GAME). The whole economy behind this game revolves around being an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, taunts are the best selling in-app purchase by a mile. If you don't live in the US (or one of the 1st world countries) then good luck trying to buy anything as the premium in-game currency price isn't region adjusted. The more you play and the farther you get (up to Diamond) the more passive and boring the game becomes. There's footsies, there's defensive oriented characters in other fighting games but this is ridiculous... some matches will be stalemates where your opponent will literally just run away. Combat in this game is challenging, but it gives you the tools to survive it.  Between seven weapon types, three combat stances for each weapon, weapon and stance-specific skills, and two support skill trees  (magic and ninjutsu) there's a lot of depth and replayability to the game, while still being accessible in that, while there's a lot of complexity, you can complete the first playthrough with learning just the basics, and then hone your skills for optional side content and the new game plus modes.

But basically, this game gives you dozens of ways to customize your character. I'd say more so than Dark Souls does. But I'm not going to say it's better than Dark Souls. It's a different type of experience. Playing this won't scratch that Dark Souls itch you may have. But I think you'll have a lot of fun anyway.

"Wow, that sounds pretty complicated. And you said this game was faster than Dark Souls as well?" Yes and yes. This game's combat is more complex, faster, combo-focused, and rewards aggressive play whereas Dark Souls is the opposite. Dark Souls is simple, slow, poke-focused, and rewards defensive play. But... that's what makes this game SO fun! This game is unashamedly about the combat whereas Dark Souls is more about the atmosphere and exploration. If you want to play a challenging, intricate, and stylish action game with fun combos then this is the game for you. I hope this clears up any confusion about whether Nioh is like Dark Souls. It's not. It is like a spiritual successor to Ninja Gaiden with Action RPG elements and... that's a good thing!

Nioh scratches your Dark Souls itch perfectly. Level design is not as good as Dark Souls but combat is more complex and fun. If you are looking for playing the game in co-op mode, then remember that it will be unlocked after beating the first boss on the ship, after around 2 hours of gameplay and a lot of deaths obviously.

At the end of it all, Nioh becomes a game MUCH easier than Dark Souls in exploration, progression, and story comprehension, but MUCH harder in the actual combat mechanics. There's a breadth of skill trees for all weapon types, three different forms for how you use them that completely change their moveset, and expansive ninjitsu/magic systems. You HAVE to know your enemies in Nioh. You will not prevail until you do, almost instinctually. It cannot be brute forced, it must be comprehended. If you are willing to embark on that quest, you'll find a much more rewarding, much more satisfying experience than any other game in the genre. If you are not willing, I don't blame you. "Nioh is hard" is an understatement.

Almost any build can survive if they are strong enough. Armor and weapon levels are much more important than keeping your favorite old one. Always go for new stuff in each region and new game cycle when you can!  Trust me, you'll thank me later.  Amazing game 9/10 on my scale.

This game is NOT dark souls and is not meant to be compared to DS. What Koei Tecmo did was create an elaborate hardcore Action/RPG with elements of looting and progression through character customization. The setting takes place in medieval japan (i believe edo period) and you play as William. Nioh is an amazingly beautiful adventure crafted in a demonic alternate history of Japan while retaining some non-fiction elements such as certain characters and locations, the combat is easy-ish to learn and hard to master while upgrading your characters skills and abilities from a good size "skill tree" to chase that build and play style that not only you love but also to eventually be able to feel confident going into battle. For those that fear "ohhh this is a game where ill be OP and itll get boring" fret not because even at high levels and huge dmg output you can still get 1 hit by even the most simple enemies. If you're into japanese culture and love a good hardcore action RPG with looting and deep style progression then Nioh is for you, personally I absolutely LOVE Nioh and can't wait for the second installment! There is however one downside to the PC version though and that is this game is meant for a controller. At least IMO because on a controller it feels so much more natural and comfortable than having to figure out what all these wonky keybindings are, and yes you can play with a keyboard and mouse but for this game i just didn't find that right. Other than that i'd have to rate this game 10/10 for the literal thousands of hours you can put into it, solid gameplay mechanics, beautiful art style and graphics and a compelling (enough) story to follow.

A RPG for action junkies. Take the level structure of a soulslike (Fromsoft games still have better level design), the loot system of a typical Diablo-style ARPG and then incorporate a combat system with as much depth and variety as the best spectacle fighters. The combat is twitchy, fast and demands you time your attacks (Like Ninja Gaiden). Each weapon is useful and fun it's just a matter of mastering them. While definitely challenging (Sometimes cheap with an overabundance of ambushes) its satisfying to play. The story is hard to follow but when your gameplay is this good the story doesn't have to be anything special. The endgame can feel more grindy then you'd like and leveling up endgame gear is an odd process of recycling gear. These don't detract from this being an amazing RPG for us twitchy masochists (Team Ninja fans)

I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 15 now. My son got this game from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 12 hours on this game. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

What keeps Nioh from reaching the hights of the game it so clearly wants to emulate (Dark Souls) is its strict adherence to strange mechanics from DS that don't carry over to this game very well.  While the games combat system (involving 3 main stances that drastically change how each and every weapon handles) is pretty unique and quite rewarding to master, this game is so needlessly covered in endless game-design word-salad that I don't feel it's worth it.  Inclusions such as bafflingly steep enemy damage (many enemies will just one-shot you with attacks that have little to no telegraph), EVERY ITEM being strictly limited (and, for the most part, one time use), and the broken Mission system that essentially allows the player to soft-lock the game at any time by picking a mission that's too hard and not being able to leave, make many sections of this game a chore.  To note, Yes, you CAN leave a mission in this game, but it is tied to a limited resource that you CANNOT get more of within a level.  This game isn’t Dark Souls hard, it's just unfair. Best description for this game would be GaidenSouls. Nicely fills the void of not having a SoulsBorne game to play. It is unique enough that it's not a complete rip off of the SoulsBorne formula and in fact expands on the combat system magnificently, with a little flavor of Tenchu. It's not just about RB/RT etc, and the stance mechanic is very rewarding once you find your favorite weapon(s) and really learn it's moveset. The variation of builds is almost endless and players are not limited by excessive (or oppressive) RNG. THE ONLY downside to this game is that it is arranged into "Missions", instead of an open seamless world like Dark Souls or Bloodborne, and there is no Invasion mechanic. Instead, players can summon Revenants, AI controlled "Invader" shades of dead players, including their skills and gear; killing them actually rewards you with the equipment they are wearing! 9/10

I don't have a lot to say here. The game has a lot of good things going for it. Combat is fast, responsive and satisfying. Armor and weapons are just as unique as in Dark Souls, especially due to the fact that the player can wield these weapons in different stances. I'm indifferent to the Ki mechanic, I guess to me it just seems kind of unnecessary. Level design is smart. Enemies are fun to fight, aside from the lack of variety. Most bosses are good fights, if not somewhat easy. Unfortunately, what ruined this game for me is the copy+pasted enemies, bosses and levels. Like I said before, all three of those things are good in their own right, but when they are shoved down the player's throat over and over again, it's hard not to get sick of it. I might like a steak once a week, but not for every meal. Farming revenants is also an incredibly annoying way to aquire new gear. Revenant fights are the same every singe time, no matter what weapon they are using, so of course it's going to get boring after the first few fights. I understand the implementation of a rarity based loot system is due to the fact that there are only 7 weapon types in the game, but I believe it could have been executed in a better way, without having the game become a total grind-fest. If your gonna make a dark souls clone then you gotta 1. do it right and 2. bring something new to the formula that you can't get in From's games. Nioh does both of these beautifully. Level design, difficulty scaling and player control are all top notch and feel right out of a From title- however Nioh isn't content to just make a feudal japan flavored souls game. It introduces an interesting mission based structure that allows the devs to remix all levels upon completion with interesting new challenges and side missions, and the H/M/L stance system allows you to have a wide variety of combat options regardless of the weapon you decide to invest skill points in. Overall a fantastic game that has skyrocketed it's sequel to one of my most anticipated titles of 2020

I have level 310 (+130) ethereal armor with graces on it and still get destroyed if I make a mistake. The balance in this game is garbage. If you play on higher difficulties get ready to die in 1-3 hits by every single enemy in the game, but if you go back to lower difficulties you 1-3 hit everything. Now the dlc for the game does nothing to solve any of these issues, as a matter of fact it takes the worst parts of the game and turns the dial up by 10. Some maps are reskins of the base game maps. You can count with one hand the number of new enemy types they introduce. Get ready for cheap and headache inducing enemy placement. Oh and don't get me started with the abomination of a map that is siege of osaka winter. Nioh is not for everyone, but it is for me. Despite the very tacked-on "Soulslike" mechanics, this game follows more in the footsteps of Ninja Gaiden than anything else. Where it fails in comparison to Soulsborne games is in enemy variety, level design, role-playing, loot, world building and atmosphere. Where it succeeds and even surpasses Souldborne is in its incredibly deep, challenging and rewarding combat, character progression, customization, memorable boss fights, and endgame content. This game is somewhat overwhelming with its sheer amount of systems at play. There's weapon proficiency, skill trees, skill/attack combo customization, weapon customization, melee and range weapons divided by tier/rarity, magic, a three stance combat system, Ki management, blessings, attributes, dojo missions to unlock skills and skill upgrades, crafting, transmogs, guardian spirits, prestige points, clans, random twilight missions, and probably much more I'm missing. It's a lot, but given enough time, you'll realize you don't need to memorize all of these things to do well. I went through the latter half of the game underleveled and still was able to beat it without much of a hassle. That said, this game is hard. Much harder than any Souls game and I've played all of them from King's Field to Elden Ring. Attacks are much faster and far more damaging. Most yokai and bosses can knock 80-90% of your health in one hit or combo. You gotta block and you gotta dodge often. Combat is much more skill-based here and you have far fewer i-frames to work with than even Sekiro. Like I said, this is more similar to Ninja Gaiden than Bloodborne. Combat is very brutal. Enemies get dismembered upon death and when you knock their ki(stamina) down to zero, it opens them up to a grapple attack. This is basically the deathblow mechanic from Sekiro, before Sekiro. The three stance system works really well for specific approaches to combat. You want maximum damage at the cost of slower attacks with high ki depletion? You use high stance. You want maximum defence? You use medium stance. You want low ki depletion with faster dodges and attacks at the cost of attack damage? You use low stance. It's quick and easy to switch between the three to maximize combat efficiency. Combos can be customized through the unlocking of skills and each weapon type has its own skill tree. The stamina management of this game is arguably the best of any soulslike game to date because of the ki pulse mechanic where depleted ki can be rapidly recovered through correctly timing the press of a button. Press too early and you only get a fraction back. Too late and you miss your chance. It genuinely becomes second nature after playing for a few hours. The game really suffers in its confusing and forgettable narrative with constant exposition for every boss/NPC you meet and will likely never meet again, and a villain who appears before almost every boss fight just to run away to the next boss fight. Disappointingly enough, he's probably the easiest boss in the game. Enemy variety is nonexistent. You will fight the same zombies, skeletons, soldiers, and handful of yokai over and over again for every single mission. Side missions are a BORE. They often take place in the exact same levels making for a monotonous grind that you don't want to do, but should for the unlocks. Level design is pretty linear which is fine, but is hampered by the forced soulslike design of having shortcuts for levels that are just too small with too little enemy variety. There's no reason to explore really given the fact that loot is randomized and there's no reason to revisit a level either. Speaking of loot, expect to have to clean up your inventory after every damn mission since you are bombarded with junk loot that's just going to be sold or disassembled. Less is sometimes more. Putting all of that aside, this is one of the few examples of a soulslike that escapes from the shadow of its inspiration by doing something unique and better in some ways. If you're looking for a great action game with decent RPG mechanics, this is your game.

The thing instead to look for in this game is the amazing combat. Unlike Dark Souls you'll have three stances you can switch to at your whim altering your attacks and movement. To go along with this is a very rewarding stamina management system, forcing your opponent to run out of their "ki" will open them up to devastating attacks. But you must be wary of the same thing yourself and strike a balance between defense and offense to keep up. Lastly the story is nothing special to wright about, so get this on sale, you won't be disappointed.

A great game with flaws that I would recommend to anyone that enjoys action games and RPGs. The combat is in depth and enjoyable. You are allowed to customize your move set which is augmented by weapon type and stances. The story is mediocre but it has some moments of charm. Throughout the game the music creates a consistent tone and does the heavy lifting to keep the player interested in the world. If you are adverse to random loot drops then this game might not be for you. However, the loot is done well; you actually have a lot of control over what you get and you can customize the stats and appearance of your equipment. On a technical level the game did crash quite a bit at a certain point, but the game saves often and the load times are fast enough that I didn't mind. The game is also a bit heavy on the side quests but if you push through it there is a fun and rewarding game to be had. There are plenty of reasons to replay it. Each new game plus offers new mechanics and you can easily try out different builds.

Through multiple playthroughs, players are granted access to higher tiers of equipment, which scales up with ever tougher enemies to be slain. The game can quickly feel very repetitive for many players. However, for players looking to get longevity out of their purchase, as well as those interested in mastery over the game mechanics, Nioh presents great value.
Highly recommended!

There are a ton of reviews for this game on Steam that give more articulate feedback than I can so I'm going to address my review to a very specific audience - Bloodborne fans.  After playing through Bloodborne a few times and absolutely loving it, I found myself wanting something new to play that was made in the same vein.  I tried the Souls games but I didn't care for the slow combat so I gave this one a shot.  I can happily report that if you just happen to be like me in that you were looking for a game that scratches that Bloodborne itch, this one scratches it nicely.   It's definitely its own game but the similarities are there.  The combat is aggressive and the Ki pulse system reminds me of the rally system from Bloodborne, only it restores Ki (stamina) instead of health so you can just keep going.  The loot is diablo styled so a lot of it won't see any use past selling or offering, but at least it's something different.  It's not a perfect game but it's definitely a good one.

Nioh is a good game. Nothing more, nothing less. The combat system is fluid, versatile, this is where newest Koei Tecmo's title really shines. Actually, Nioh ruined Dark Souls combat for me, which now seems sluggish and slow...it's just hard to come back to DkS after playing this. All the other aspects of the game - graphics, sound, world design etc. - are just decent. The worst thing about Nioh is that it quickly becomes repetitive and recycling of monsters and levels in later missions is very noticeable. It lacks visual diversity, atmosphere of secrecy and deep lore, in some places it's even dull and uninspired. Story is also rather meh...Subsequent playthroughs are not worth it - just simple grind fests with a bit of frustration. In a nutshell, buy it if you like difficult, fast action games, just don't expect Soul's or Bloodborne's level of greatness, Nioh is nowhere as tight or addicting.

So let's start from a new players point-of-view. You have unlocked your first planet. You can continue to do the mission-nodes that it has to offer, all the way up to the planet boss. Each planet also has a newly-added feature, which are known as Junctions. Junctions are what players have to go through to get to the next planet, and will offer a variety of trials before passage. Upon completing a Junction, you are rewarded with a few things, such as blueprints for weapons, a few parts for building a few specific warframes, and they will unlock quests. Quests are side-things that you can do, which also give you some rewards. There are a handful of warframes that are quest-exclusive if you want to obtain them, as well as some helpful items to assist you along the way. Another recent addition (as in since December) are Cinematic Quests. These are main story-related quests that have cutscenes, and usually have a lot to reveal about the lore, and will unlock some other nice things (You still have to unlock these quests from Junctions, or even just through the market.) The in-game market shows mostly all of everything you can get in the game. The best part? You can get most of this for free! Of course you can add money to just BUY weapons, warframes, gear, companions, etc., and gain access to them immediately, but this is not a pay-to-win game. Not at all. It's more of a 'pay-to-progress-faster' game. However, building these things by yourself without paying any real currency can be a fun time-consuming process. The word Fun can be taken literally or sarcastically in this subject, depending on what the building requirements are, for what you are making. You gather resources to build and complete these things from different planets throughout the solar system, each having their own set of different resources. They drop from enemies, loot lockers, and storage containers (there is even a warframe that increases loot drops, while simutaneously punching souls and raising the dead!). Also, you can earn the real-money currency in this game by trading with other players. I'm out of space at this point, but all I have to say is I wish more of my friends could get into this.

However, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to potential new players. The on-boarding experience, while improved over the years is still pretty bad. They teach you the gameplay well enough, but then throw you into a frankenstein's monster of systems that they did not put nearly enough effort into explaining. There are also so many vestigial systems. As a new player, you might find yourself pouring in time to understand one of these bastardized systems to only to find out that it's out-dated and been unsupported for years. (looking at you archwings among other things) They really could stand to invest some time and money into improving the onboarding experience for new players. Clean up/remove unused systems, optimize the current ones and create worthwhile tutorials for them. New content is great for us who have played for hundreds of hours, but I feel like they would do themselves more good if they spent some extra time and money on the early game. There is a reason only 40% of players have gotten to the 2 hour mark of this game and this is the biggest reason why. I wish this was a game I could recommend to not only others on steam, but to my friend group. As it stands now, I cannot.

Warframe has come a long way from when i first started playing, but i can honestly say the majority of it was great! Let me start by describing what warframe is. Its an over the shoulder third-person shooter where you play the role of a ninja warrior in space. The solar system is in chaos, and it's up to you to maintain the balance. With many weapon types to choose from, and different frames to use to suit your playstyle, the possibilities are endless. However there are certain strategies in higher level missions that even veteran players will tell you work. It's pretty much an MMO at this point, so certain "classes" of warframes work better at farming resources on certain missions. The developers also release new content as operations to introduce the new features, for example, the newest addition was corpus dropships that drop squads of enemies into battle. It was introduced as Operation: Ambulas Reborn, which featured a reworked boss that dropped in from the ship with a squad of regular enemies. There were a few bugs at first, but the incredibly awesome support team was very quick to respond to reports and get back within 24-48 hours. All in all, this has become one of the best free to play games i have ever played, and the graphics do an excellent job of immersing you in a living, breathing world that is constantly changing. I have to say that there are certain aspects of the game which require you to pay for features. Such as certain weapons, cosmetic packs, etc. Other than that, if you work hard and spend a decent amount of time on it, everything important is attainable without paying money for it. I do encourage you to support the developers by buying things that you may like, but only at your own discretion. Speaking of which, there is also a thriving market for the ingame currency, platinum, where you can spend platinum to buy parts, weapon mods, and other hard to obtain aspects from other players, as well as selling your own parts and mods to other players to obtain platinum. The prices will indeed vary on the rarity of what you are trying to get, but there is also sites and a wiki for any questions you may have about said things. All in all i have had a great experience with this game, rather than reading my long-winded review about the game, why not try it yourself? It's free! Also feel free to add me ingame and i will do my best to be as helpful as possible, my name is Mix_Masterson. See you on the battlefield, and have fun!

After playing it for 92 days on Xbox and now 300 some odd here on steam, I gotta say Warframe is a pretty good game, could it be better, yes, but you can say that about any game in the world, now that doesn't mean I don't think Warframe needs imporvements, like the constant content drought that happens with the game, or the fact that many updates and new additions to the game are more so tailored to new players, rather than adding true end game content that the veterans that have been playing for thousands and thousands of hours desperately need rather than having to go in and see how long they can make it in a survival because they have simply ran out of things to grind for at a certain point. But even still I always find myself returning to Warframe, as a person who normally doesnt enjoy the full hard grind mmo action style games, because at a certain point I get bored of the repetitive nature of them and want to move onto something else, but Warframe has and continues to be a game that breaks that trend for me, as I started playing back in 2014 after a friend who played the game on pc told me about it and I figured I'd give it a shot, and from there the game had managed to hook me, with its flowing movement system, diverse roster or frames and weapons that you can play with, and the overall level of freedom and power the game lets you feel. And while you can feel the grind while you are working towards increasing your mastery rank, or trying to farm out that last 1000 plastids to get a new weapon, it still feels satisfying to do so, simply because even though the mission type are generally quite similar, the weapons and combat of the game are just fun to play with, whether you run around with a big ass sword and cut down people from the waist, or you use a weapon with the dreaded self damage, just so you can see your enemies get blown sky high. Or you use a punch through tonkor because you want to use an explosive weapon, but you don't want to actually use an explosive weapon. Its all fun to just ♥♥♥♥ around with and see what ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you can get up to trying out different builds. And all of this just cumulates into an experience that is fun to play and refreshing from the normal monotony that is most grinding mmos. Also DE themselves as a company is fantastic, providing feedback to their community, constantly keeping in touch with us, and making sure we know what they are getting up to, trying their best to keep us happy. So overall I would say its definetly a game to check out, and learn more about, because it appeals to those that enjoy grind games and those that don't.

It's a good game. It's the absolute best game that you can get as a F2P game. It's always engaging to dissolve a whole wave of enemies in a single attack.

But what about the game itself? Well, in general I’m not a huge fan of the F2P model (there are one or two notable exceptions). Usually the developers struggle to make it work. But Warframe is probably as good an example of this type of game as you’re likely to find these days. In many respects DE have got it right. It is possible to play completely for free, although I would encourage players to buy some Platinum (I have) as DE deserves to make a buck or two for all their hard work. Playing for free can put you at a slight disadvantage, but only when playing with players who’ve bought higher level weapons and frames. Success lies more in the mods you have available, and how you use them, than in anything else. Personally, I’ve only used my Platinum to buy additional inventory slots, as a large part of Warframe is the farming for, and building of new gear. And here’s where the grind comes in. It goes on and on and on, and, as I’ve said, it can be both tedious and frustrating. Warframe is also the most complicated game I’ve ever played, mainly, I suspect due to its having been developed and modified over such a long period. Be prepared to spend a lot of time trying to fathom out what the hell you’re supposed to do. And then there’s the gameplay itself: this is where Warframe scores most highly. The movement and combat mechanics are excellent. Every weapon (and there are so many of them) has a unique feel. Lots of them are just levelling up fodder but they’re all fun to use. The same applies to the frames, of which there are approximately 60 (at time of writing). Of course there are keepers in amongst the chaff and these weapons and frames bring the most enjoyment. The parkour-style movement is well implemented and very satisfying once you get the hang of it. The mission types are limited but the main story line does offer some relief from the routine and is deeper and more fleshed-out than the stories found in many AAA paid-for games. The community is good for the most part: a “git gud” attitude does exist to some extent but it’s not prevalent. All in all Warframe is an impressive achievement: It’s a well-designed game with lots of content and it offers a good deal of enjoyment. It’s just a shame that it’s marred by the dispiriting grind. Recommended with the above qualifications. I thank you!

For a game in it's beta version it is actually quite impressive. This game is a 3rd person co-op shooter game featuring (the generic definition) "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ space ninjas with magic." There is a large variation of characters to fit anyones play style including various and very unique and powerful energy abilities and weapons. The game excels in graphics, level design, and combat keeping the game very dynamic with the best experience making this one of the best free-to-play game in existence.

The community is also very friendly and helpful. One of my favorite things to do in the game is Tridolon hunting. It's incredibly satisfying to take down these powerful enemies in a short amount of time and it gives a sense of accomplishment. Overall, Warframe is an enjoyable and fulfilling game that I highly recommend.

While it's a VERY good MMO, and I have to enphasize this, it's excellently made, very detailed, the graphics are awesome, the theme is rather unique, it's also an EXTREMELY complicated game that can bog you down very quickly and very easily. It has practically zero tutorials, you're just flung in the deep end and told to swim, and that's the easiest of complications. Being this detailed and unique leaves the player with no actual frame of reference, even if you're a gamer and an MMO player. You need to "translate" all the otherworldiness into normal MMO terminology "oh, this is the raids, this is the skill training, this is for pets", so in order to find out what you need to do and how you either need someone else who knows the game to explain things to you or to spend many hours reading the wiki. Also it has thousands of different "currencies", all for different things, to buy things, to upgrade things, to modify things, to buy premium things, to do whatever, and it seems that everything has its own currency and you need to navigate through that too. You can extremely easily screw up, and get left without knowing what's next. If you're not ready to put that kind of commitment into it, I suggest you skip it, and herein lies the game's main problem: you have to really love it to play it, but you need to have played it to love it. So, it's no wonder it's rather dead on overall. Personally I found the gatekeeping everything behind "mastery ranks" very tedious, on top of all the rest of the complications.

Warframe is a free to play co-op or solo third person shooter. This game obviously had A LOT of work put into it, which is why I do not understand why it is free. It has outstanding graphics, even on the lowest setting. However, this game in some aspects has a "pay to win" feel to it. To be able to get new items and characters in which they call "Warframes", you can either buy them with real life money, or invest immense amounts of hours into the game to get them, which isn't that bad at all because the game is really fun. The gameplay is terrific, and the given ability to free roam each individual map is superlative. Each map has different objectives, environments, and climates, whether its to the inside of an enemy ship, a snowy mountain, or some abnormal planet. If you're looking for a new game to play, that's free and not to mention fun, then Warframe is most definitely the game for you! If you heard any previous bad reviews about this game, just remember, it has improved a lot since its release date back in March.
In all seriousness it is a good game with good devs. good players. best memes.

Alrighty, so I rarely leave reviews, but quite frankly, at this point I feel like I should. Ive poured my soul into this game and its been a fantastic run. This game has outstanding graphics and the optimization is solid. The gameplay and the in-game movement and parkour is a really fun addition to the game and really makes the game fast paced (at most times; the game still does have its dull moments). For a free to play game, youre getting so much gameplay and you can really pour some serious time into this game (currently at 1,804 hours atm). The game isnt without its flaws though. There are a few bugs that irritate the heck out of me such as mission waypoints bugging out and not displaying properly or the rare moments of falling through the map when deploying my K-Drive. Even with all the bugs though, I always find myself coming back to this game. The customization is also really something else. You have so many different options for skins, armor pieces and colors that you really can make your warframes stand out even amongst the same frames. The modding system (upgrade system) is also really extensive. If you really like a frame, you can mod it to the way you want to play so you can really excel at what you do. You can pretty much tune your frame to the way you want to play so theres so much freedom with making your builds. There's so much more I could say about this game but all im going to say is its definitely worth the time (and money) ive put into it. If youre on the fence on whether you should get it, give it a chance. Theres very little tutorial but if you find a helpful higher MR player thats willing to show you the ropes, give it some time. You will get it. You will want to join a clan early on for the extra tech that you get from being in one. Well, thats all i have to say for now. Good luck Tenno!

There’s no sense of lethality or badassery going on when your character feels like they’re made of soggy toilet paper while enemies can last through an entire magazine of gunfire. Warframe understands this, so every frame feels fun to play, because every frame has powerful, over-the-top capabilities.

You play as a Tenno, a person psychically linked to one of several bio-mechanical surrogate bodies known as Warframes. These enhanced bodies are capable of incredibly acrobatic feats and superhuman strength. So, in essence, you control a sci-fi ninja who hacks, slashes, and shoots the many looming threats that encroach upon the galaxy. The reward is the loot used to improve your arsenal, improve your Warframes, and of course, improve your look,Warframe is a mission-based game, for the most part, that tasks you with visiting various planets to defeat genetically modified humanoid warmongers, giant robots, and other threats that present themselves as you make headway through the story. The missions include target assassinations, escorting or saving NPCs, collecting a key item, or fighting a major boss character. In nearly each mission, your Warframe slices, dices, and blasts any grunts that get between you and your target. There is a modicum of strategy to the carnage, though. Levels have a fantastic degree of verticality thanks, and even enclosed environments incorporate multi-level architecture and alternative paths, giving you a choice as to whether you want to rush in guns blazing or sneak through stages to avoid alarms and rack up stealth kills,Warframe's combat doesn't resemble Devil May Cry or Ninja Gaiden's juggle-based action, but there's so much gameplay flourish that it could easily be lumped together with said titles. In many respects, the action carries a Platinum Games flair. As in Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, Warframe gives you a basic melee combo string, an auto-deflect tactic against ballistics that activates while running, and a shocking degree of mobility and speed. Warframes can seamlessly slide, dash, wall-jump, and double-jump, and they can go straight into an attack or shot at any point during these actions. It feels good.

Dead by Daylight is not a game. It is a cosmic punishment sent by indifferent gods to remind humanity of its insignificance. Booting it up is like willingly inserting your face into a malfunctioning wood chipper. Nothing makes sense. Hitboxes defy physics. Perks do not function unless you chant in Latin. Killers phase through walls like demonic glitches. Survivors collapse into puddles of incompetence the moment a heartbeat sounds. Every match is a dissertation in disappointment, a Shakespearean tragedy written by drunken raccoons on fire. You don't play Dead by Daylight you endure it, like a prisoner endures solitary confinement, counting the cracks in the wall until madness becomes your only friend. Updates break more than they fix, a perpetual motion machine of failure. Pallets fly away into the sky. Generators burst into flames because a moth sneezed on them. Flashlights either stun the killer or open a black hole on the map, no in between. Queue times feel longer than the lifespan of stars. And the reward for surviving? More blood points so you can suffer again. Again. And again. This game has personally lowered my IQ. My dreams are skill checks now. My hands tremble when I hear the Entity’s noise. If Dante had known about Dead by Daylight, there would have been a Tenth Circle of Hell and THIS would be the only thing playing. I would rather be force-fed glass by a rabid moose than ever install this corrupt, festering, soul-devouring, sadness-engine ever again. Dead by Daylight isn’t a horror game. It’s a warning. A cursed artifact. It is a SCREAM into the VOID and the VOID screams back.

So I decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, did the tutorial but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Grandson for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my grandson since I'm no longer chairman of the parish council. This game has ever since brought my grandson and I closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my grandson many happy memories.

This game has truly been a very memorable journey, there is definitely a good, a bad, and an ugly to this game. I personally feel Dead by Daylight is a must play for horror fans or people who just want a good scare every now and then or be the people who want to scare others!. Dead by Daylight is without a doubt not a perfect game as most aren't, but I believe every penny I spent on this game was well worth it. I wouldn't even mind paying full price. Within Dead by Daylight you'll come across so many different types of people while playing; people who care for each other even if they are just strangers just trying to accomplish the same goal survive, people who are complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that will make you feel like an idiot for almost no reason, people that are poor sports ETC disconnecting from the game if something doesn't go their way or feel something that the killer did was not fair (which sometimes can be understood if you too see it as a good reason). People who you can relate with, have a good laugh and even become lifelong best friends, you will also come across people who you wonder are even on the same planet as you in terms of how they appear on profile/act in game. If you plan on buying this I'd suggest making sure that you are a good sport; don't just follow one survivor at a time until they die (tunneling), don't drop pallets onto other survivors that didn't do anything wrong (exception for playing with friends wanting to see them die and if they agree to trying to fight you off during the match along with the killer trying to kill your team), don't call people meaningless stupid names after the match is done its just unnecessary negative energy that nobody deserves/needs. In all the years I have spent playing video games, I have never been more upset and disappointed at a development team than I am at BHVR. I have put almost 3,000 hours into this game playing both killer and survivor because it's actually fun, unique, and addicting. You can play a range of killers that all have unique powers and have their place in the game, or you can play as a survivor with some bomb ass cosmetics. Not to mention the licensing from popular classic horror movies and video games. There is no other game out there that can compete with Dead by Daylight.  However, with each new patch that is released, it has become apparent that the devs do not care about their community. They add killers whose powers are unbalanced, perks that are broken and unfun for both sides, and matchmaking has been in a state of misery making solo q survivor unbearable and killer boringly easy. Each patch is met with new cosmetics and random changes that no one asked for rather than addressing bugs that are game breaking. On top of this, the feedback they receive on their changes are completely ignored. What is the point of releasing a PTB and gathering feedback if none of it matters, and they're going to release the changes anyway? No one wanted graphical updates. No one enjoyed being forced to kick breakable walls to break infinites that have been reintroduced to maps. No one enjoys being hit from 10m away because of desync. No one wanted a new HUD. No one wanted new movement. It hurts to see a development team willingly kill their game because they simply don't care what their community has to say about it when their community is what is keeping the game alive. I have put almost 3,000 hours into this game because I love it, and now I regret ever buying it. Save yourself the trouble, and do not buy this game until the devs show they actually deserve the money you are about to give them.

The learning curve is pretty high. It's understandable to be frustrated at first or find it difficult. If you decide it isn't for you, there is no shame in that. You tried to enjoy the game, and time is valuable. It might be better for you to spend it somewhere else if you are not getting value from the game. However, if you still want to stick with it, I will say just continue playing. Experience will help greatly as you learn the maps and different perks.

The majority of your skill depends on your strategies, reflexes and looping/mind gaming. Although all of them can be affected by perks, your baseline skill is what will win trials. Early on, certain healing/aura/exhaustion perks will help as you get used to the game. No matter what you end up with at the start, try adapting so you can learn to use all>any>no perks, it’s silly and lots of fun. Perks cause play style variety that adds flavour otherwise it’s like playing a time management sim whilst being chased down by a scary monster. 👍👍

Dead by Daylight is a wonderful game, just not for beginners. It is one of the worst multiplayer games to pick up and play due to the sheer amount of knowledge required just to get started, and the lack of a competent tutorial does NOT help. However, if one is willing to suffer for a few hundred hours to get to an average skill level, Dead by Daylight can be one of the most fun and in depth multiplayer games out there. The infinite techs and nuances surrounding each and every killer allow for thousands of hours of niche mechanical and strategic development that very few games can offer. After accruing nearly 2k hours across both Steam and Console, I often still find myself learning new things about the game, and even the killer that I specialize in, and have put hundreds of hours into mastering. Overall, Dead by Daylight is a great game for someone that is seeking a (VERY) challenging but rewarding experience.
Even though, i'm gonna keep playing it because at the end, i like it.

The premise and implementation of the game is great, and I understand that it's ridiculously hard to balance a game of this nature to where the majority of players are pleased. There's a reason why so many people have pumped hundreds, if not thousands, of hours into this game. The Devs are visible, they try to keep the community informed, and are always releasing new content, which is great, but I believe that more focus needs to be put into ensuring the core of the game is perfected first. If you're new, you're in for a rough ride, but it gets better, and much more enjoyable. There's alot of great aspects to the game, which makes it worth spending time in. Releasing exclusive content for specific regions creates an artificial division between players, undermines the sense of community unity, and generates dissatisfaction. Apparently, they have already earned enough money, and they no longer need it. And such a simple idea that it is necessary to unite people, not divide them, is apparently too difficult for Bhvr. This Game is essentially Murder: The Hide and Seek Video Game. You have two sides in each match, survivors, and killers. One killer hunts down four survivors, and one killer has to do the job as such. They(The survivors) don't get any weapons and will have to escape using perks (skills, running faster for 3 seconds with a 40-60 second cooldown) or items like flashlights (blinds and stuns the killer so he can't see you run away for around 5 seconds or so.) They can also drop what are called 'pallets' onto killer players which are found in tight corners or open spaces to give more distance, as the killer has to spend time breaking it or going around to get to you again. However, they do have an advantage. The second that you run you leave little red 'scratch marks' on the ground that lead the killer to you. Most of the time when you are hit, you will be put into the wounded state, meaning you limp around while crying and drop blood, the killer can follow that blood directly to you, so the main job is to hide and not be found, as the longer you're chased the more disadvantages you'll have (Such as the killer attaining bloodlust, which makes him move way faster, on top of them already moving faster than you in the first place). It's not designed to be a fair 1v1 experience, it's designed to be a 4v1, and as such the killer is much stronger than a survivor and as such can easily beat them after a short time and put on a hook. If you get hung on a hook you have a certain amount of time to get off before the game kills you. Known as 'stages' each time you're on the hook you'll progress a stage, or if you're on too long. There's three stages. The first you can get out of the hook with ease, the second you'll have to mash spacebar constantly to avoid going into three, someone will have to rescue you before you die. It's a VERY fun game with a wide variety of options and ways to have fun. Don't be worried about the 'toxic community' as the only time the enemy team can even talk to you is post-match if you're killer, and as survivor only for the first few seconds before the match starts. During the game no contact can be made by or to either side, making the tension and teamwork a requirement. I heavily recommend this game if you have friends and plan to play survivor, or if you don't and want to be a killer. Being a survivor alone isn't that bad. People say that you'll get tunneled (The only survivor the killer hunts) and die, and while this is true, it doesn't matter at all. What tactics are employed by either side are a part of the game (Save the occasionally patched exploit.) In all, this is a very fun game for people who casually play games, or people who seriously play games. It doesn't matter how you enjoy games, there's a place here for you. If you're concerned about salty or toxic people just don't read the pre/post-game chat and you won't see problems. (Yes, tbagging can happen to you as killer but in that case just camp their hook and kill them, as killer you have the option to do whatever you please with them, and 'winning' is entirely subjective.) Ranks are the only real 'reason' to win the game, if that's what you really want in a hide-and-seek game go for it. Bloodpoints will be rewarded either way, and the amount is based on the 'feats' you pull off in-game, not your rank nor rank up materials. The game is wonky and absolutely unfair to survivors/killers at times, but both sides always have options of dealing with this, there's no reason to complain about it, it's just fun. Play it for fun, not for ranking. It's a Hide and Seek game for crying out loud, just enjoy yourself!

Alors là chapeau, j'ai acheté ce jeu car j'aime la survie et le craft ,celui-ci avait l'air fun en plus,fonds marins , jolis décors etc et bien je suis cloué. Ce jeu n'arrète pas de me surprendre, je vais de découverte en surprise, dire que ce jeu est complet,le mot est faible. Je m'explique, au premier abord on plonge dans les fonds marins d'une planète inconnu avec sa faune et sa flore  . Après avoir survecu au crash de votre mèga vaisseau spatial , vous devez survivre à bord de votre capsule de survie que vous allez devoir réparer . Mais là ou cela devient interessant, c'est que plus vous découvrez d'espèces d'animaux et de plantes, plus vous trouvez de débris de vaisseaux ou autres engins, plus vous apprennez à fabriquer d'objet , de vehicules ou de base sous-marine . Je suis très loin d'avoir tout découvert malgré mes 20h de jeu et c'est déjà très prenant . Les biomes sous-marins sont très variés et plus ou moins profond ( jusqu'à + de 650 m ) habissal ! La construction de votre base sous-marine se doit de respecter les lois de la pression , plus elle sera profonde , plus il y a de risque que la pression de l'eau ouvre des breches dans la coque ou fissure les vitres etc . Bref, dire qu'il faut survivre avec tout çà ! La map est géante , le craft juste énorme , la découverte je suis bluffé , je suis fan . Addictif .
CONCLUSION : Si vous aimez les aventures se déroulant dans le milieu aquatique Subnautica est vraiment un jeu incontournable avec une ambiance irrésistible !

Dead Space.Comment: Best game in 2008, best game in 2023
Ce remake est une pure dinguerie, le gameplay, la technique. Du beau travail de passionnés.

En somme, ce remake n’est pas qu’un hommage : c’est un véritable chef-d’œuvre, une lettre d’amour aux fans de l’original et une porte d’entrée idéale pour les nouveaux joueurs. Dead Space Remake est la preuve qu’un jeu culte peut être modernisé tout en restant fidèle à son héritage. Si vous aimez les survival horror, c'est tout simplement incontournable.

En tout cas le jeu est magnifique, casi pas de bug juste 1 cinématique bugger pour ma part le reste niquel et les graphismes époustouflant et aucun lag (j'ai un AMD Ryzen 5 et une 3070 RTX actuellement). En tout cas je recommande ce jeu l'histoire est vrm cool mais l'immersion est incroyable et surtout les jeux de lumieres puis la bande son palala, je pense que c'est un des très bon jeux que j'ai joué de ma carriere de geek qui maitrise la bande son et les jeux de lumieres casi parfaitement.

Le jeu est vraiment beau en ultra et ça surprend comme à l'époque. Je modifie mon évaluation ayant fini le jeu, j'en suis arrivé à bout en 15h de jeu, ce qui est très honnête pour un jeu de ce style, les petites chutes de fps ont pour la plupart été corrigées mais pas toutes ce qui laisse supposer que d'autres patchs arriveront. Il s'agit d'un véritable remake, où certaines choses se passent différemment, le jeu est plus cohérent dans sa généralité (Par exemple par l'apparition de Pnj etc... on est seuls mais tout n'est pas tout à fait décimé à notre arrivée sur l'Ishimura, rajout de profondeur sur certains personnages) Je note aussi que malgré qu'EA soit l'éditeur, au lancement du jeu il ne demande même pas de me connecter à Origin, je suppose que ça passe entièrement par Steam et ça sa fait plaisir (Avec tous ces launchers différents, ça file la gerbe). Le jeu est vraiment une version ++ du Dead Space de l'époque et vaut vraiment le coup même si l'ont à déjà fait celui de l'époque.
** Je vous conseille de faire  des sauvegardes souvent.
OUI AU REMAKE 2ET 3 ET PEUT ETRE 4

Mais on y retrouve aussi tout ce qui avait déjà fait le succès de Dead Space en 2008, et plus encore : l'immersion est totale (notamment grâce à l'absence de HUD et de temps de chargement), la bande originale efficace, et le design sonore contribue à instaurer un climat de terreur permanent (ça peut se traduire par un cri à glacer le sang qui surgit de nulle part, le râle d'une créature tapie dans l'ombre ou la simple respiration de notre personnage qui tranche avec le silence environnant). Malgré la déferlante de créatures affreuses qui défilent à l'écran, l'essentiel de la peur se transmet par le son. La mécanique de démembrement, qui consiste à viser les articulations des ennemis pour en venir à bout plus facilement, a été remise au goût du jour : une fois couplée aux nouveaux modes de tir secondaires et aux autres pouvoirs de Clarke, qui peut aussi ralentir ses ennemis à grand renfort de stase et déplacer des objets par télékinésie, chaque combat devient une fête (une fête qui tourne au vinaigre, avec des convives qui rampent au plafond et qui explosent au contact, mais une fête quand même). Pour le reste, le remake n'est pas parfait pour autant, les environnements auraient pu être encore plus beaux (même si les lumières sont toujours sublimes), les zones de non gravité encore plus plaisantes à jouer, les menus un peu plus attrayants. Mais pour tous les amoureux du premier, et les amateurs du genre qui auraient eu la chance de passer à côté, c'est une œuvre faite avec beaucoup d'amour, qui se permet constamment de tutoyer les étoiles.

Minecraft Dungeons is a very simplified take on the formula popularized by Diablo. Skill trees and direct stat customization are out, with most abilities and offensive options being determined by loot to a greater degree than similar games. For those new to the genre or those otherwise looking for a breezier version of it, particularly children, Minecraft Dungeons should be a solid experience, but more experienced players may be left in want by its lack of apparent depth.

En terme de conduite, les équipes de Playground Games ont procédé à quelques affinements. La physique générale du jeu a été modifiée, en particulier les suspensions, pour rendre le comportement des voitures plus proche de la réalité. Sans parler de simulation, loin de là, les véhicules ont un comportement plus cohérent par rapport à leurs homologues réels. Si cela peut laisser présager d’un pilotage plus pointu et exigeant sur le papier, manette en main, le constat est tout autre. La conduite est ici plus souple, plus intuitive et, surtout, plus agréable que dans le volet précédent. Au final, la conduite offre de bonnes sensations, tout en gagnant en accessibilité. Abordons maintenant le gameplay, qui se présente comme une expérience tout aussi réussite. La diversité des véhicules (plus de 800), des supercars aux bolides tout-terrain, offre une variété de sensations de conduite. La physique réaliste et le souci du détail dans la modélisation des voitures procurent une expérience authentique et immersive. Les nombreuses activités et défis répartis dans le monde ouvert obligent d'y jouer des dizaines et dizaines d'heures et garantisses une certaine durée de vie dans le temps du jeu, garantissant des heures de jeu sans l'ombre d'une monotonie et, personnellement donnant la sensation d'avoir vraiment bien dépensé son argent dans ce jeu!
Si ils arrivent à corriger ça sur leur prochain volet ou même dans un patch (on rêve un peu) alors ce Forza Horizon 5 sera surement l'un des meilleurs jeux de course de voiture arcade possible.
Enfin pour FH6 j'ai beaucoup d'attente des devs pour qu'ils nous proposent un jeu qui pourrait améliorer tout les points qui nuisent à ce jeux.

Bon alors, commençons par ma config, avant que certains ne disent que cela vient de mon PC qui ne serait éventuellement pas assez puissant. Je possède une RTX 3080 neuve, un Ryzen 9 neuf, 32Go de RAM, une B550F neuve, et un watercooling neuf.... bref un monstre en sois, je fais tourner tous les dernier jeux qui demandes énormément à fond en 2k à plus de 110-120 FPS constant, dont Forza Horizon 4 lol évidemment. J'ai joué au 1, 2, 3, 4 mais le 5..., mon Dieu le 5.... Le 5 est d'une infamie sans nom, bourré de bugs en tous genre et surtout graphiques sur PC, c'est injouable, il marche 1 fois sur 2 car quand on le lance des fois le jeu décide de tourner à 4 FPS constant (vrai anecdote), et d'autres il veut bien marcher mais avec une qualité graphique immonde (j'ai déjà réglé le problème de la mise en échelle de la résolution mais c'est impossible que le jeu soit comme je le vois graphiquement je ne veux pas le croire, dans ce cas les rabats joie qui disent que FH4 est plus beau ont presque raison). Donc voilà la liste est encore longue avec les vibrations qui ne marchent que 1 fois sur 4 avec la manette ou bien le curseur de la souris qui ne veut pas s’enlever... Bref, en attente d'un bon patch sinon c'est remboursement direct malheureusement

I want to say this game is good, I really do, I love playing it, and I love being in the game racing. But I feel like this game could be a LOT better with next to no effort from the development team. They could fix the unbalanced cars and instantly make the game 100x more fun to play online. They could remove cheated leaderboard scores & make getting the highest score mean something. They could actually add unique cars to the region, or listen to their damn community, but they won't. This feels like a "safe profit" game. A game manhandled by some execs into losing its soul just so it could be an easy game to profit from. It feels corporate, its not the same horizon you had as a child/teen on your xbox 360, and its not the same game as the previous title. Its a soulless husk of a game within a series that was at one point the greatest open world racing experience. I'm still going to play it, its one of the only open-world racing games & I dont exactly have a choice to fill that niche. I want this game to be the best it can be, but it really feels like i've joined just as the ship was going down. Good Graphics wont save a game with an awful experience, and this has been a champion of awful experiences lately.
